entities.title: Compact text under a token budget, paged
entities.summary: Tools return plain text lines, never JSON, stop at a budget of max_tokens × 4 bytes (at least 256) or a result limit, and end with a footer that says how many there were or which offset or start line comes next.
entities.context: Every byte a tool returns is read by the agent and costs tokens; the tools exist so agents spend fewer than with grep and cat.
entities.decision: Output accumulates lines until the budget is reached; each listing tool takes limit or max_results and offset and prints a footer such as "[n of m; next offset k]"; read prints "[truncated; continue with start_line n]".
entities.rationale: The tools are offered in place of raw commands (search's and read's descriptions say they replace grep, rg, cat, head, tail and sed -n), so they must cost the agent fewer tokens; the usage log records est_tokens (bytes / 4) for every call so that can be checked.
entities.origin: The search and read tool descriptions; AGENTS.md ("Write code for low token use"). Until commit 5ea503c the hook's search message also called the tools cheaper in tokens.

entities.title: Label every answer that did not come from the index
entities.summary: Each call records in the usage log how its answer was produced (path) and why (reason): index, scan / index_cold, fallback:rg or fallback:git-grep / regex_unsupported, run:<program> / passthrough, run:git / git, view.
entities.context: The tools are meant to be shaped by real use; the owner needs to see how often the index could not answer, and why.
entities.decision: Tools set CallInfo.Path and CallInfo.Reason; McpServer writes them into the usage log, and zazzle-csharp-indexer report groups calls by them. The external regex fallback also says so in its footer, and run adds a hint when a dedicated tool would have done; an index_cold scan is not mentioned in the answer (backlog.json, index-cold-unlabelled).
entities.rationale: Without the label, slow or degraded answers would be indistinguishable from indexed ones in the report.

entities.title: Hand patterns .NET rejects to an external PCRE engine
entities.summary: When .NET cannot compile a non-literal pattern, search runs rg -P, or git grep -P when rg is not installed, in each root.
entities.context: Agents write Perl- and PCRE-style patterns; some constructs (possessive quantifiers, recursion, \K) are not .NET syntax.
entities.decision: SearchTool.Run catches the compile error and calls ExternalSearch.Try; if the external engine also fails (exit code above 1), the agent gets bad_regex with notes on the .NET dialect.
entities.rationale: The agent gets an answer rather than an error, and the log shows how often it happens (reason regex_unsupported).

entities.title: Keep a guarded passthrough instead of refusing unforeseen questions
entities.summary: run lets the agent execute read-only commands through the server, so questions the tools do not cover still get answered and logged; its allowlist guards against agent mistakes, not hostile agents.
entities.context: No fixed set of tools covers every question; an agent that is refused falls back to its shell, where nothing is logged.
entities.decision: RunTool runs argv without a shell after RunPolicy.Check; the user may lift the policy with run.unrestricted.
entities.rationale: From the code's own comments: so unforeseen questions still go through the server and get logged; the policy guards against agent mistakes, not hostile agents. zazzle-csharp-indexer report lists the run commands as candidates for new tools.

entities.title: What the indexer's own read and search tools are for now that zazzle is the front door
entities.summary: The server's instructions, init's snippet and the redirect hook now send agents to zazzle to read, search and list files and to the indexer only for C# structure, but tools/list still offers search, read, find_files, outline and run, whose descriptions say they replace grep, cat and find.
entities.context: Since commit 5ea503c, McpServer's instructions say to read, search and edit through zazzle and to use the indexer for overview, find_symbol, find_references, changed_since, git_log and git_blame; init's snippet says the same, and HookPolicy names zazzle_find, zazzle_ls and zazzle_read instead of search, find_files and read, and no longer mentions report_gap. McpServer still lists all thirteen tools to every client. search's description says it replaces grep and rg, read's that it replaces cat, head, tail and sed -n, find_files' that it replaces find and ls, and run's that it is the fallback when they cannot answer and report_gap says what was missing. An agent with both servers sees two sets of read and search tools with conflicting advice, and the usage-shaped improvement loop now hears of gaps only from agents that read run's or report_gap's own description. zazzle has its own zazzle_outline beside the indexer's outline.

options.title: Keep every tool as it is
options.consequences: Nothing changes for clients that use the indexer alone; agents with zazzle get conflicting advice about which read and search tools to use.

options.title: Reword the overlapping tools' descriptions to defer to zazzle
options.consequences: One consistent message; the tools stay for clients without zazzle.

options.title: Stop listing the overlapping tools to MCP clients
options.consequences: A smaller tool list; view, which zazzled calls by name, and the structure tools stay. Clients without zazzle lose read and search, and run and report_gap need a new place, or an end.

blocks.description: Whether gap reports still come from agents depends on whether report_gap stays advertised.

origin.description: Raised while bringing the indexer's .dev files in line with commit 5ea503c, from the difference between McpServer.Instructions, HookPolicy's messages and the tool descriptions.
